CBB.what_it_is: Bacterial infection causing angular brown leaf spots and wilting.
immediate: Prune and remove all visibly infected leaves immediately.
Disinfect pruning tools with bleach solution (1 part bleach : 9 parts water) between plants.
Do NOT compost infected leaves — burn or bury them far from the field.
treatment: Spray copper-based bactericide (e.g., copper oxychloride) every 10–14 days.
Improve field drainage — CBB spreads faster in waterlogged soil.
Apply balanced NPK fertilizer to strengthen plant immunity.
prevention: Rotate with maize or legumes for at least one season.
Avoid overhead watering — water at the base.
CBB.expert_note: If more than 30% of your field is infected, contact your local agricultural extension officer — the field may need to be replaced with clean cuttings.

CBSD.what_it_is: Viral disease causing brown streaks on stems and rotting of the tuber — the biggest threat to cassava in East Africa.
immediate: Uproot and destroy infected plants IMMEDIATELY — including the roots.
Do NOT eat or sell roots from infected plants — they may be toxic.
Do NOT take cuttings from any plant showing symptoms — this spreads the virus.
treatment: There is NO cure once a plant is infected.
Only clean, certified virus-free cuttings from approved sources should be planted.
Control whiteflies (the virus carriers) with neem-based sprays every 7 days.
prevention: Source cuttings ONLY from certified clean seed programs.
Plant CBSD-resistant varieties where available (e.g., Narocass 1).
Inspect new plants weekly for the first 3 months — early detection saves the field.
CBSD.expert_note: CBSD spreads fast. If you see more than 2–3 infected plants, contact your extension officer the SAME WEEK. Delaying can lose the entire crop.

CGM.what_it_is: Tiny mites feeding on young leaves, causing yellow speckling and stunted growth.
immediate: Inspect the underside of young leaves — mites hide there.
Spray neem oil solution (5 ml neem oil + 1 L water + 1 drop soap) on affected plants.
treatment: Use insecticidal soap on heavily infested plants.
Introduce predatory mites (Typhlodromalus aripo) — available through extension programs.
Remove alternate host weeds around the field.
prevention: Avoid drought stress — healthy plants resist mites better.
Mulch around plants to retain soil moisture.
Plant early in the rainy season.
CGM.expert_note: CGM rarely kills plants alone, but weakened plants become vulnerable to other diseases. Treat early.

CMD.what_it_is: Viral disease causing yellow-green mosaic patterns on leaves, reducing yield by up to 70%.
immediate: Remove and burn infected plants within 3 days of noticing symptoms.
Do NOT take cuttings from infected plants — the virus passes to the next generation.
Wash hands and tools after handling infected plants.
treatment: There is NO cure for CMD once a plant is infected.
Control whiteflies (spreaders of the virus) with neem spray or yellow sticky traps.
Focus on protecting healthy plants in the field.
prevention: Rogue (remove) infected plants weekly during the first 3 months.
Use certified virus-free cuttings from trusted sources.
CMD.expert_note: CMD is endemic in East Africa. Every farmer should rogue at least once a week — 5 minutes a week saves a harvest.

Healthy.what_it_is: No disease detected — your cassava leaf looks healthy.
immediate: No action needed — your plant is healthy! ✅
Keep monitoring weekly for early signs of disease.
treatment: Continue your current crop management practices.
prevention: Maintain regular weeding and good field hygiene.
Inspect new growth weekly, especially during rainy season.
Use clean tools and certified cuttings for any new planting.
Healthy.expert_note: Early detection is the best protection. Keep scanning your crop weekly with CropGuard AI.
